title: Ind AS 8 "Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors"
outcomes: Select accounting policies, including where no Ind AS applies.
Account for changes in accounting policies.
Account for changes in accounting estimates.

meta.exam_tip: First label the item — policy, estimate or error — and the treatment follows almost automatically.

concepts.title: Selecting and applying accounting policies
body: Accounting policies are the particular principles and practices an entity has chosen for preparing and presenting its statements. Where an Ind AS applies to an item, its requirements (with application guidance that forms part of it) are followed.

Where no Ind AS applies, management uses judgement to develop a policy that gives relevant and reliable information, referring in order to: Ind AS dealing with similar issues; then the definitions, recognition criteria and measurement concepts in the Conceptual Framework. Management may also consider the most recent pronouncements of the IASB, and of other standard-setters with a similar framework, accepted industry practice and literature, if consistent with the above.
Policies are applied consistently to similar transactions unless an Ind AS requires or permits categorisation with different policies.
concepts.analogy: When the rulebook is silent, Ind AS 8 tells you where to look and in what order.
concepts.work: A company accounting for a new kind of carbon credit first looks for a similar Ind AS before using the Framework.

concepts.title: Changes in accounting policies
body: A policy is changed only if an Ind AS requires it, or if the change results in reliable and more relevant information. Applying a policy to new transactions that differ in substance, or that were immaterial before, is not a change in policy.

A change from an Ind AS is applied using its transitional provisions; otherwise retrospectively, by adjusting the opening equity of the earliest period presented and restating comparatives, as if the new policy had always applied.

If retrospective application is impracticable for particular periods, the change is applied from the earliest period for which it is practicable; if not practicable at all, prospectively from the earliest practicable date. Disclosures include the nature, reasons and amounts of adjustment. The initial application of a revaluation policy under Ind AS 16 or Ind AS 38 is dealt with as a revaluation under those standards, not under Ind AS 8.
concepts.analogy: A policy change rewrites history so that every period presented is on the same basis.
concepts.work: Switching from FIFO to weighted average cost requires restating comparative inventory and cost of sales.

concepts.title: Changes in accounting estimates
body: Accounting estimates are monetary amounts in the statements subject to measurement uncertainty — e.g. expected credit losses, net realisable value, fair values, useful lives and depreciation patterns, warranty provisions. They are developed using measurement techniques and inputs.

A change in estimate results from new information or developments and is not a correction of an error. Its effect is recognised prospectively in profit or loss of the period of change and future periods affected, or by adjusting the related asset, liability or equity item.

When it is difficult to tell whether a change is in policy or estimate, it is treated as a change in estimate. Changing a measurement technique or input is a change in estimate unless it corrects an error.
concepts.analogy: Estimates are updated going forward; they never reopen past periods.
concepts.work: Revising the expected warranty rate from 2% to 3% affects this year's provision only.

concepts.title: Prior period errors
body: Prior period errors are omissions or misstatements in past statements from failure to use, or misuse of, reliable information that was available and could reasonably have been obtained — including mathematical mistakes, misapplying policies, oversights, misinterpretation and fraud.

Material errors are corrected retrospectively in the first set of statements approved after discovery: restating comparatives for the period in which the error occurred, or, where the error is older, adjusting the opening assets, liabilities and equity of the first period shown.

If impracticable, correction is from the earliest practicable date. Disclosures cover the nature of the error, the correction for each line item and EPS for each prior period presented, and the correction at the beginning of the earliest period. Hindsight is not used when estimating amounts for prior periods.
concepts.analogy: Errors are fixed in the past where they happened, not hidden in this year's profit.
concepts.work: An unrecorded sales return discovered next year is corrected by restating last year's revenue.

illustrations.title: Life of a machine revised
illustrations.q: A machine cost ₹100 lakh, life 10 years, nil residual, straight-line. At the start of year 4 management concludes the total useful life is only 8 years. Compute depreciation for year 4 and explain the treatment.

head: Step
Working
₹ lakh
rows: Carrying amount at start of year 4
solution.title: Change in accounting estimate

solution.text: This is a change in estimate — applied prospectively from year 4. Earlier years are not restated; the effect is disclosed.

checks.label: Carrying amount at start of year 4 (₹ lakh)

illustrations.title: Correcting last year's error
illustrations.q: While preparing 2026-27 statements, Ruby Ltd. discovers that depreciation of ₹10 lakh for 2025-26 was omitted (material). Tax rate 25%; assume the tax effect is a deferred tax adjustment. How is it corrected and what is the effect on retained earnings at 1 April 2026?

head: Item
Correction in comparative 2025-26 figures
rows: Reduce deferred tax liability (or create asset) by ₹2.5 lakh; tax expense down ₹2.5 lakh
solution.title: Retrospective restatement

solution.text: The correction is made in the first statements approved after discovery by restating comparatives; it is not passed through 2026-27 profit. A third balance sheet may be needed if the opening position of the comparative period is materially affected.

checks.label: Reduction in 2025-26 profit after tax (₹ lakh)

jobs.title: Is it a policy, estimate or error?
jobs.situation: The client proposes several year-end "adjustments" to last year's figures.
steps: Classify each as policy change, estimate change or error.
Check the justification for any policy change.
jobs.takeaway: Classification decides whether comparatives are restated — get it right first.

mcqs.q: Where no Ind AS applies, management first refers to:
options: Ind AS dealing with similar and related issues
mcqs.explain: The hierarchy starts with analogous Ind AS, then the Framework; other sources may be considered if consistent. In practice: document the judgement.

mcqs.q: A voluntary change in accounting policy is allowed only if it:
options: Gives reliable and more relevant information
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 8 permits voluntary changes only on this ground. In practice: disclose reasons.

mcqs.q: Changing a depreciation method from straight-line to diminishing balance is treated as:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 16 treats it as a change in estimate, applied prospectively. In practice: reflects changed pattern of consumption.

mcqs.q: A change in accounting estimate is applied:
mcqs.explain: Effects are recognised in the current and future periods. In practice: disclose the effect if practicable.

mcqs.q: A material prior period error is corrected:
options: Retrospectively in the first statements approved after discovery
mcqs.explain: Comparatives or opening balances are restated. In practice: disclose line-item effects.

mcqs.q: Applying a policy to transactions that differ in substance from earlier ones is:
options: Not a change in accounting policy
mcqs.explain: New kinds of transactions need a policy; that is not a change. In practice: disclose the new policy.

mcqs.q: If it is unclear whether a change is in policy or estimate, it is treated as:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 8 resolves doubt in favour of estimate treatment. In practice: prospective application.

mcqs.q: First adoption of the revaluation model for PPE is accounted for:
options: As a revaluation under Ind AS 16, not under Ind AS 8
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 8 excludes this from its retrospective rules. In practice: revaluation surplus goes to OCI.

summary: Hierarchy: Ind AS → similar Ind AS → Framework → other pronouncements (if consistent).
Policy change: required or more relevant; retrospective unless impracticable.
Errors: retrospective in first statements after discovery.
remember: New types of transactions are not policy changes.
traps: Depreciation method change is an estimate change.

viva.q: When can an entity change an accounting policy?
viva.model: When an Ind AS requires it, or when the change produces reliable and more relevant information.

viva.q: How is a change in policy applied?
viva.model: Retrospectively, adjusting opening equity of the earliest period presented and restating comparatives, unless transitional provisions or impracticability apply.
A monetary amount in the statements that involves measurement uncertainty, such as an expected credit loss, useful life or provision.

viva.q: What is a prior period error?
viva.model: An omission or misstatement in earlier statements caused by failing to use, or misusing, reliable information that was available when those statements were approved.

viva.q: Can hindsight be used when restating prior periods?
viva.model: Hindsight is avoided; estimates for prior periods reflect information that existed at that time.

cases.title: Granite Pharma Ltd.
cases.case: Granite Pharma Ltd. (year ending 31 March 2027) finds: (i) the expected credit loss rate on receivables needs revision from 2% to 4% due to new market data; (ii) last year's inventory was overstated by ₹15 crore owing to a counting error (material); (iii) it decides to change from FIFO to weighted average because it reflects consumption better; (iv) it starts leasing out a building for the first time and adopts the cost model for investment property.

options: A change in estimate, applied prospectively
mcqs.explain: New information changes the estimate. In practice: adjust the current-year allowance.
A material prior period error is corrected retrospectively. In practice: last year's cost of sales rises.

options: A voluntary change in accounting policy applied retrospectively
mcqs.explain: Inventory cost formula is a policy; voluntary change needs more relevant information and is retrospective. In practice: disclose reasons.

options: Not a change in policy — a new type of transaction
mcqs.explain: Applying a policy to transactions not previously occurring is not a change. In practice: disclose the new policy.
